_comment: Batch 09 (Sets 16-17). Distractor-only rewrites to remove the longest-answer cue. Correct options, stems, and rationales are unchanged; each distractor keeps its original meaning and stays wrong for the same reason.

RN-S16-02.B: A client admitted yesterday with an acute MI who is now pain-free on continuous telemetry
RN-S16-02.C: A client receiving an insulin infusion for DKA whose glucose is now 210 mg/dL
RN-S16-02.D: A client with a new chest tube for a pneumothorax placed earlier today

RN-S16-03.B: A client newly admitted with chest pain who needs a complete admission assessment and a 12-lead ECG
RN-S16-03.C: A client receiving a blood transfusion for the first time who has a history of heart failure
RN-S16-03.D: A client with a new diagnosis of diabetes who needs a discharge teaching plan developed today

RN-S16-04.A: "Take everyone's vital signs this morning and write them on the whiteboard at the nurses' station when you're finished with the rounds."
RN-S16-04.C: "Check the vitals on all of your clients when you have time this morning, and chart them before lunch."
RN-S16-04.D: "Go ahead and take vitals on your assigned clients, and just let me know if anything seems off to you."

RN-S16-06.A: Report the AP to the nurse manager immediately for refusing the assignment
RN-S16-06.C: Complete the task yourself and say nothing to the AP about it
RN-S16-06.D: Discuss the problem at the next team huddle in front of the others

RN-S16-07.A: Explain the surgery in detail yourself and then have the client sign the consent
RN-S16-07.C: Have a family member who is present sign the consent form instead
RN-S16-07.D: Tell the client that the doctor knows best and that the surgery is needed

RN-S16-08.A: Withhold the antibiotics because the client has a DNR order and therefore does not want any aggressive treatment
RN-S16-08.C: Stop all nursing care and treatments, since a DNR order means the client should be kept comfortable only
RN-S16-08.D: Transfer the client to hospice care without discussing it with the client or the family

RN-S16-10.A: Apply restraints to keep the client in bed until the provider arrives to talk with the client about the risks
RN-S16-10.C: Take the client's clothes and belongings to keep the client from leaving the unit
RN-S16-10.D: Call security to stand at the door and prevent the client from leaving the hospital

RN-S16-11.A: Write "incident report completed" in the client's medical record after the fall
RN-S16-11.C: Include opinions about who was at fault and how the fall could have been prevented
RN-S16-11.D: Give the client a copy of the completed incident report for their records

RN-S16-12.A: Cover the error with correction fluid, let it dry completely, and then rewrite the correct entry neatly
RN-S16-12.C: Tear out the page with the error and carefully recopy all of the entries onto a new page
RN-S16-12.D: Scribble over the entry completely so that it can't be read, then rewrite it

RN-S16-13.A: A nurse gives a medication exactly as prescribed, and the client has an unexpected allergic reaction to the very first dose
RN-S16-13.C: A client refuses a treatment after the nurse explains the risks, and the client's condition later worsens
RN-S16-13.D: A nurse follows the facility's policy for a procedure exactly as written, and the client has a known complication

RN-S16-14.A: Ignore the behavior in order to avoid conflict with the coworker
RN-S16-14.C: Cover the coworker's client assignment for the shift and say nothing about it
RN-S16-14.D: Post about the coworker's behavior on the nurse's social media page

RN-S16-16.A: "This is Jane, the nurse caring for Mr. Lee in Room 12. I'm calling about his breathing."
RN-S16-16.B: "His SpO2 dropped to 88% on 2 L, and he has new crackles in both lung bases."
RN-S16-16.C: "He was admitted 2 days ago with pneumonia and has a history of heart failure."

RN-S16-18.A: To identify which nurse made the error so that the nurse can be disciplined or retrained by the manager
RN-S16-18.C: To gather information that the facility's lawyers can use to prepare for a possible lawsuit
RN-S16-18.D: To document all of the details of the event in the client's permanent medical record

RN-S16-24.B: Increase the oxygen flow to 6 L/min by nasal cannula and then recheck the client's SpO2 level
RN-S16-24.C: Call the provider to report the change in condition before assessing the client
RN-S16-24.D: Obtain a sputum specimen for culture and sensitivity before giving antibiotics

RN-S17-01.A: Aim at the top of the flames, pull the pin, squeeze the handle, and hold the nozzle still
RN-S17-01.C: Squeeze the handle, pull the pin, sweep side to side, and then aim at the fire
RN-S17-01.D: Sweep the nozzle side to side, aim at the fire, pull the pin, and squeeze the handle

RN-S17-03.A: Wrap the frayed area of the cord with electrical tape and continue using the pump
RN-S17-03.C: Continue using the pump until the end of the shift, then report the cord
RN-S17-03.D: Unplug the pump only while the client is sleeping, then plug it back in

RN-S17-04.A: The evening before surgery, when the surgeon visits the client to review the procedure and answer questions
RN-S17-04.C: During recovery in the PACU, once the client is awake enough to answer questions
RN-S17-04.D: Only if the surgeon requests it, or if there is a question about the surgical site

RN-S17-05.A: Document the count discrepancy in the operative record and let the surgical team close the incision as originally planned
RN-S17-05.C: Assume the missing sponge was thrown away in the trash and note it in the operative record
RN-S17-05.D: Ignore the discrepancy if only one sponge is missing and the surgeon is ready to close

RN-S17-08.A: The client showers with chlorhexidine soap the night before and the morning of surgery
RN-S17-08.C: Prophylactic antibiotics are given within 60 minutes before the surgical incision
RN-S17-08.D: Normothermia is maintained during surgery with a forced-air warming blanket

RN-S17-09.A: Airborne precautions in negative-pressure rooms, with N95 respirators for all staff
RN-S17-09.C: Droplet precautions with surgical masks for all staff and visitors who enter
RN-S17-09.D: Strict reverse (protective) isolation in private rooms with HEPA filtration

RN-S17-11.A: Wipe up the spill right away with paper towels and throw the towels in the regular trash can in the room
RN-S17-11.C: Pour plenty of water on the spill to dilute it, then mop the area until it is completely dry
RN-S17-11.D: Leave the spill for housekeeping to clean up without warning anyone in the area

RN-S17-12.A: Put on regular exam gloves, clean up the spill with paper towels, and throw them in the regular trash can
RN-S17-12.C: Mop up the spill with the unit's regular mop and a bucket of warm, soapy water right away
RN-S17-12.D: Ask the client's family members who are visiting to help clean up the spill quickly

RN-S17-14.A: "Set your water heater to 140°F (60°C) so the water stays hot enough to kill germs."
RN-S17-14.C: "Use a heating pad set on high while you sleep to ease your joint pain."
RN-S17-14.D: "Remove the smoke detector batteries if the alarms keep going off by mistake."

RN-S17-15.A: Try to take the knife away from the visitor quickly, before anyone in the hallway gets hurt
RN-S17-15.C: Stay close to the visitor and argue with them to convince them to calm down and put the knife down on the floor
RN-S17-15.D: Continue with the assigned client care and assume that security will handle the situation on their own

RN-S17-16.A: Standard precautions only, with routine daily cleaning of the room using quaternary ammonium
RN-S17-16.C: Droplet precautions only, with a surgical mask for anyone entering the room
RN-S17-16.D: No special precautions are needed, because the client is only colonized and not infected

RN-S17-17.A: "It protects you against both hepatitis A and hepatitis C, so you won't need to get any other hepatitis vaccines during your nursing career."
RN-S17-17.C: "The vaccine is only needed for operating room staff, since they handle blood and sharp instruments every day during procedures."
RN-S17-17.D: "Once you're vaccinated, you won't need to use standard precautions such as gloves when you handle blood or body fluids."

RN-S17-18.A: Wait about 1 hour to see whether the client returns to the room on their own before taking any action
RN-S17-18.C: Call the client's family at home to ask whether the client left with them earlier today
RN-S17-18.D: Document the client's absence in the medical record and continue with the 1400 rounds

RN-S17-19.A: Override the alert and give the medication as scheduled on the MAR
RN-S17-19.C: Scan the medication again and again until the alert clears
RN-S17-19.D: Give the medication now and report the alert to pharmacy later

RN-S17-24.A: Leave the client's room right away to call the provider and request a prescription for restraints
RN-S17-24.C: Apply soft wrist restraints right away to keep the client from climbing out of bed
RN-S17-24.D: Administer the PRN haloperidol that is prescribed for agitation and recheck in 30 minutes

PN-S16-01.A: Administering scheduled oral medications to a stable client with a chronic illness
PN-S16-01.B: Reinforcing discharge teaching that the RN has already started with a client
PN-S16-01.D: Collecting data on a client's wound during a scheduled dressing change

PN-S16-03.A: Document the BP value in the resident's chart and continue the rounds
PN-S16-03.C: Tell the AP to recheck the resident's BP in 4 hours and report back
PN-S16-03.D: Give the resident's scheduled antihypertensive medication on time

PN-S16-04.B: A resident requesting help to make a phone call to a family member
PN-S16-04.C: A resident who is due for a scheduled daily multivitamin with breakfast
PN-S16-04.D: A resident who wants a snack and a glass of juice before lunch

PN-S16-05.A: Completing each task in the exact order in which the clients use their call lights throughout the shift
PN-S16-05.C: Saving all of the documentation until the end of the shift, when it is quieter
PN-S16-05.D: Skipping meal and rest breaks in order to finish all of the assigned care on time

PN-S16-06.A: Give the medication as ordered, because the provider is the one responsible for the prescription and its safety
PN-S16-06.C: Change the dose to an amount that seems safer and document the reason for the change in the record
PN-S16-06.D: Explain the concern to the client and ask whether they still want to take the medication as ordered

PN-S16-07.A: Share the information about the resident's condition, since the caller says he is a family member and sounds very concerned
PN-S16-07.C: Give the caller only the resident's diagnosis, but not any other details about the resident's care
PN-S16-07.D: Hang up on the caller without giving any explanation, since it may not really be the resident's nephew

PN-S16-08.A: "Proud to be a nurse!" posted with a selfie of the nurse in uniform and no client information
PN-S16-08.C: A post sharing a public health article about flu vaccines from the CDC website
PN-S16-08.D: A post about attending a nursing conference, with a photo of the convention center

PN-S16-09.A: "Client seems very depressed again today and doesn't want to do anything, which is the client's usual behavior."
PN-S16-09.C: "Client had a really bad day today and was in a poor mood during most of the shift."
PN-S16-09.D: "Client is being difficult and very uncooperative with the staff about meals again."

PN-S16-10.A: Document the dressing change using the original time, as if it had been charted right on time 3 hours ago
PN-S16-10.C: Skip documenting it, since the dressing change has already been completed and the wound looked fine
PN-S16-10.D: Ask a coworker who is less busy right now to document the dressing change in the chart for you

PN-S16-11.A: The nursing staff caring for the resident
PN-S16-11.C: Any family member who visits regularly

PN-S16-12.A: Witness the signature, since the client is still able to hold the pen and sign the form on their own
PN-S16-12.C: Have the client's spouse sign the consent form instead while the client rests in bed
PN-S16-12.D: Sign the consent form for the client, since the client already agreed to the surgery

PN-S16-13.A: "You need to take your bath right now, because it's on the schedule for this morning."
PN-S16-13.C: Give the bath anyway, since the resident is scheduled for one this morning
PN-S16-13.D: Report the resident to the RN for being uncooperative with morning care

PN-S16-14.A: Confront the son about the bruises on the resident's wrists the next time he visits
PN-S16-14.C: Wait to see whether more bruises appear over the next week before reporting anything
PN-S16-14.D: Ask the resident to keep a written diary of each visit from the son and what happens

PN-S16-15.A: Attempt the procedure after watching an online video about how to do it
PN-S16-15.C: Refuse the assignment and leave the unit for the rest of the shift
PN-S16-15.D: Ask the AP to perform the procedure instead, with the nurse nearby

PN-S16-16.A: The resident's favorite TV shows and the snack the resident prefers at bedtime
PN-S16-16.C: The nurse's personal opinion of the resident's family members and their visits
PN-S16-16.D: Every routine task that was completed during the shift, listed in time order

PN-S16-17.A: Apply a vest restraint so the resident stays in bed safely through the night
PN-S16-17.C: Raise all four side rails on the bed so the resident is unable to climb out during the night
PN-S16-17.D: Give the resident a sedative from the stock supply without a provider's order

PN-S16-19.A: Tell the client to eat whatever is served, since the kitchen prepares the same meals for all of the clients on the unit
PN-S16-19.C: Tell the client to have family members bring in all meals from home during the stay
PN-S16-19.D: Remove the meat from the tray without asking the client and serve the rest of the meal

PN-S16-20.A: Have the client's 12-year-old child, who speaks English well, interpret
PN-S16-20.C: Speak more loudly and slowly in English and use simple words
PN-S16-20.D: Give the client detailed written instructions printed in English

PN-S16-21.A: Continue the resident's home medication list without reviewing it, since the resident was taking those same medications before the hospital stay
PN-S16-21.C: Start only the new medications that were prescribed in the hospital and stop all of the resident's previous ones
PN-S16-21.D: Ask the resident which of the medications they would like to continue, and give only those that the resident chooses

PN-S16-22.A: Say nothing to the coworker in order to avoid conflict, since it was most likely a one-time mistake on a busy day
PN-S16-22.C: Post about the coworker's behavior anonymously online to raise awareness about hand hygiene
PN-S16-22.D: Tell the client that the coworker did not wash their hands after leaving the room

PN-S16-23.A: Accept the parent's explanation and document that the child stepped in hot bathwater
PN-S16-23.C: Ask the parent to explain again how the injury happened, then decide what to do
PN-S16-23.D: Wait until the child's next clinic visit to see whether the burns are healing

PN-S17-02.A: It is always required by policy for residents who are confused or at risk of falling
PN-S17-02.C: It makes the bed and the side rails harder for housekeeping staff to clean thoroughly
PN-S17-02.D: It prevents the nursing staff from reaching the resident quickly enough to provide care during the night

PN-S17-05.A: "Store all of your medications together in unlabeled containers to save space in the bathroom cabinet."
PN-S17-05.C: "Take your medications in the dark at night so you don't wake up your spouse."
PN-S17-05.D: "Share your medications with your spouse if either of you runs out before a refill."

PN-S17-06.A: Place the belt loosely around the client's chest, just under the arms, before helping the client to stand and walk
PN-S17-06.C: Hold the client firmly by the arm instead of using the belt while walking in the hall
PN-S17-06.D: Use the belt to lift a client who cannot bear weight from the bed into the chair

PN-S17-07.A: Place the wheelchair on the client's left side with the brakes unlocked so that it can be moved closer
PN-S17-07.C: Have the client pull on the armrests of the wheelchair to stand up from the bed
PN-S17-07.D: Place the wheelchair facing away from the bed with the footrests in the down position

PN-S17-08.A: Operate the lift by yourself to save time when the unit is short-staffed during mealtimes
PN-S17-08.C: Lift the client high above the bed so the sling clears the side rails easily
PN-S17-08.D: Leave the client suspended in the sling while getting supplies from the room

PN-S17-10.A: Administering oral medications to a client
PN-S17-10.C: Giving a cleansing enema before surgery
PN-S17-10.D: Feeding a client with a weak swallow

PN-S17-11.A: Shake the linens gently over the floor to remove crumbs and debris before placing them in the bag
PN-S17-11.C: Place the soiled linens on the floor next to the bed until the bed change is finished
PN-S17-11.D: Carry the soiled linens against the body to the hamper at the end of the hall

PN-S17-12.A: The regular trash can in the client's bathroom, double-bagged
PN-S17-12.C: A puncture-resistant sharps container in the room
PN-S17-12.D: The recycling bin in the clean utility room

PN-S17-13.A: Wipe up the blood with a dry paper towel, throw the towel away, and leave the area to air dry
PN-S17-13.C: Cover the spill with a towel and wait for housekeeping to come and clean it, without warning anyone else in the area
PN-S17-13.D: Mop the area with plain water only and then dry the floor with a clean towel from the linen cart

PN-S17-14.A: No additional PPE is needed beyond the gloves
PN-S17-14.C: Sterile booties worn over the shoes
PN-S17-14.D: An N95 respirator only, with no gown

PN-S17-15.B: Cancel the radiology test until the client no longer needs droplet precautions
PN-S17-15.C: Have the transport staff wear N95 respirators and leave the client unmasked during the trip
PN-S17-15.D: No precautions are needed once the client is outside of the isolation room

PN-S17-16.A: Well-cooked chicken breast with steamed white rice
PN-S17-16.C: Pasteurized yogurt and low-fat cottage cheese
PN-S17-16.D: Washed fresh fruit, such as apples and pears

PN-S17-17.A: "Keep it loaded in a nightstand drawer for quick access at night."
PN-S17-17.C: "Hide it under the mattress where the children can't see it."
PN-S17-17.D: "Teach your young children how to handle and use the gun safely."

PN-S17-19.A: Give the medications as scheduled, since the nurse knows the client well from caring for them on previous shifts
PN-S17-19.C: Ask the client's roommate to confirm the client's full name and then give the medications as scheduled
PN-S17-19.D: Use the room number and bed number on the assignment sheet to identify the client before giving medications

PN-S17-20.A: Ignore the client's report, since the allergy isn't documented anywhere in the chart
PN-S17-20.C: Give the penicillin if it is prescribed, since there is no allergy band and no allergy documented in the chart
PN-S17-20.D: Tell the client to remind every nurse about the allergy before taking any medication

PN-S17-21.A: Leave the client's metal hair clips in place during the scan so that the client's long hair stays out of the way
PN-S17-21.C: Send a portable metal oxygen tank with the client for the trip so oxygen is available in the MRI room
PN-S17-21.D: Apply the client's nicotine patch with a foil backing before the client leaves the unit

PN-S17-22.A: Spending as much time as possible in the room with the client
PN-S17-22.C: Standing close to the implant site while providing care
PN-S17-22.D: Assigning the same pregnant nurse to the client every day

PN-S17-23.A: "About 1 cup of water per person per day is enough."
PN-S17-23.C: "Only bottled soda is needed for drinking in an emergency."
PN-S17-23.D: "Water isn't needed as long as you have canned food stored."
